heading: F# waits for a typed answer from a real Yon endpoint
summary: An F# HTTPClient is a type with only abstract members, such as `abstract read: unit -> Task<Greeting>`. Tachyon writes each member and reads the answer into the record `Greeting` from `client/models`. A member may also answer a list or an array of records, a plain value, `BehaviorJSON`, nothing (`Task`) or a `ValueTask`. An answer of another shape raises a `BehaviorError` whose `Code` is `HTTP_RESPONSE`, and a failed request raises the code of the browser transport, such as `HTTP_STATUS`. A service gets the client from a settable property with `[<Needs>]` above it; the page does not see this property, and a service takes at most five clients. A service member may return `Task` or `ValueTask` of the same kinds of values, and the page gets a promise that settles when the task ends. While the task waits for the server, the page keeps working. `GreetingSetup` adds no adapter, so the request goes to the server of the page: the same origin, without cookies. `Cached` lets the browser cache answer a read, and after a successful `ClearCache` the next read asks the server again. `OverrideSetup` gives `OverrideClient` its own adapter, an F# object expression, and that adapter answers instead of the network. Removing the component cancels the request, and the promise is rejected with the code `CANCELLED`. The server half of this example is a plain JavaScript controller. A controller in TypeScript, Python, PHP, Java, Groovy, C#, F#, Kotlin, Rust, Go, Dart, Ruby, Lua or C++ answers in the same way (see Controllers), so this section shows only the browser side in other languages.
